name: libpgm
desc: Implements the PGM reliable multicast protocol
why: An implementation of PGM reliable multicast, an obscure protocol door, though it is mostly a library to link against.

brief.what_it_is: A Homebrew formula called libpgm, described as implementing the PGM reliable multicast protocol. Its homepage is the steve-o/openpgm GitHub repository, whose About line says it is an automatically exported copy of the code.google.com/p/openpgm project. The scout notes describe it as mostly a library to link against rather than a command-line tool. I could not read the README, so I cannot confirm the inputs, outputs, or API from the source.
brief.why_it_exists: The README text was not retrieved, so the author's framing is unknown. The formula description says only that it implements the PGM reliable multicast protocol.
brief.install_notes: The formula lists no executables, so it installs a library rather than a command. I did not see build steps, dependencies, or configuration in the pages I could read.
brief.standout: Scout notes call PGM an obscure protocol, so the appeal is probably that a reliable multicast implementation is rare to find packaged. This is inferred from the scout notes and the formula description, not from the README.
brief.status: unknown. The repository page shows 1,252 commits, 63 stars, 41 forks and 6 watchers, but no last-commit date or release date was visible in the HTML. The repo is also an automated export from Google Code, which suggests the upstream project is older.
brief.caveats: The homepage is a GitHub repo, and the fetch returned page chrome rather than the README, so the README and docs were not read. The Homebrew formula name (libpgm) differs from the repository name (openpgm). Nothing in the pages I read covers platform support or license, so check the repo's LICENSE file before writing about it.
